exercises.name: variables1
exercises.hint:
A variable must be declared before use: put a type (or `var`) in front of the name.
    int x = 5;

exercises.name: variables2
exercises.hint:
Give `number` a starting value when you declare it, e.g. `int number = 42;`
It has to be bigger than 10 for the check to pass.

exercises.name: variables3
exercises.hint:
A `const` can never be changed after it's declared.
Remove `const` to make `score` a normal variable.

exercises.name: variables4
exercises.hint:
Match each value to its type:
  19.99m → decimal, true → bool, 'D' → char,
  "Hello" → string, 8_100_000_000 → long, -3.5 → double

exercises.name: variables5
exercises.hint:
Use int.Parse(input) to turn text into an int.
Cast with (int)average to drop the decimals.
Use count.ToString() to turn a number into text.

exercises.name: if1
if2
exercises.hint:
Look at the boundaries: is a 12-year-old a child? (the rule says *under* 12)
Is a 65-year-old a senior? (the rule says 65 *or older*: >=)
The student check doesn't need the `|| age < 12` part at all.

exercises.name: switch1
exercises.hint:
Every case section needs a `break;` at the end — add one after `result = "weekend";`.
Then add `case "Tuesday":` ... `case "Friday":` sharing one body, and a `default:` section.

exercises.name: loops1
exercises.hint:
A for loop header has three parts: for (int i = 1; i <= 100; i++)
In the while loop, count each halving with halvings++;

exercises.name: loops2
fizzbuzz
exercises.hint:
Check the 'both' case first: a number divisible by 3 AND 5 is divisible by 15 (n % 15 == 0).
If you checked n % 3 first, 15 would return "Fizz".
The fallback is n.ToString().

exercises.name: strings1
strings2
exercises.hint:
raw.Trim(), trimmed.ToUpper(), trimmed.Length, trimmed.Contains("C#"), trimmed[0], trimmed.Replace("fun", "awesome").
For the range: "C#" starts at index 9 (count from 0!), and the end of a range is exclusive: trimmed[9..11].

exercises.name: strings3
exercises.hint:
In the loop: sb.Append(i); then if (i < 5) sb.Append('-');
For the fruits: string.Join(", ", fruits)

exercises.name: strings4
exercises.hint:
orderLine.Split(';') gives you { "Keyboard", "3", "49.99" }.
Parse with int.Parse(parts[1]) and decimal.Parse(parts[2]).
A $ inside an interpolated string is just a normal character: $"{quantity} x {product} = ${total}"
For the JSON: $$"""{"product": "{{product}}", "quantity": {{quantity}}}"""

exercises.name: methods1
exercises.hint:
Greet doesn't return anything, so its return type is `void`.
Square takes a whole number: `int n`.
Average returns a decimal number: `double`.

exercises.name: methods2
exercises.hint:
IsEven: n % 2 == 0
Describe: a string on its own line does nothing — you need `return "even";`.
Clamp: add `return value;` at the end for the normal case.

exercises.name: methods3
methods4
methods5
exercises.hint:
The return type is a tuple with names: (int Min, int Max, double Average)
To deconstruct: var (lo, hi, avg) = Stats(...);

exercises.name: arrays1
exercises.hint:
planets[0], planets[^1], planets.Length, planets[..4]
The loop bug: valid indexes go from 0 to Length - 1, so the condition should be i < squares.Length.

exercises.name: lists1
exercises.hint:
todo.Add("write code"); ... then todo.Insert(0, "drink coffee"); then todo.Remove("test code");
For evens: foreach over numbers, and evens.Add(n) when n % 2 == 0.

exercises.name: dictionaries1
collections1
exercises.hint:
HasDuplicates: foreach value, if (!seen.Add(v)) return true;
Queue: line.Dequeue()
IsBalanced: compare `open` with the opening version of `c` — e.g. if c is ')' then open must be '('.
At the end, return stack.Count == 0 (anything left over was never closed).

exercises.name: quiz1
exercises.hint:
Average: guard against Count == 0 first, then sum in a loop and return (double)sum / scores.Count.
Letter: check the highest grade first: if (average >= 90) return "A"; ...
Report: copy the keys into a list (new List<string>(gradebook.Keys)), Sort() it, build each line with $"{name}: {avg:F1} ({Letter(avg)})", and string.Join("\n", lines).

exercises.name: exceptions2
exceptions3
quiz2
exercises.hint:
Start with the interface and InsufficientFundsException, then Account, then SavingsAccount.
Keep a private List<string> for history, and expose it as IReadOnlyList<string> History => _history;
Use `public decimal Balance { get; private set; }`.
Mark Account.Withdraw `virtual`; SavingsAccount overrides it, counts withdrawals, and calls base.Withdraw(amount).
ApplyInterest can simply call Deposit(Balance * InterestRate).

numbers.Where(n => n > 10).ToList()
numbers.Select(n => n * 2).ToList()
numbers.Where(n => n % 2 == 0).Select(n => $"#{n}").ToList()
words.Select(w => w.Trim()).Where(w => w.Length > 0).Select(w => w.ToUpper()).ToArray()

exercises.name: linq2
exercises.hint:
staff.OrderByDescending(e => e.Salary).Select(e => e.Name).ToList()
.OrderBy(e => e.Department).ThenBy(e => e.Name)
First(...) vs FirstOrDefault(...)
Any(e => e.Years < 3), All(...), Count(...), Where(...).Sum(e => e.Salary)
Top 2: OrderByDescending(...).Take(2).Average(e => e.Salary)

exercises.name: linq3
exercises.hint:
1. sales.GroupBy(s => s.Region).ToDictionary(g => g.Key, g => g.Sum(s => s.Quantity * s.UnitPrice))
2. .Select(s => s.Product).Distinct().Order().ToList()
3. .GroupBy(s => s.Product).Select(g => (g.Key, g.Sum(s => s.Quantity))).OrderByDescending(t => t.Item2).ToList()
4. orders.SelectMany(o => o).Sum()

exercises.name: linq4
exercises.hint:
from c in customers where c.City != "London" orderby c.Name select c.Name
from o in orders join c in customers on o.CustomerId equals c.Id where o.Total > 30 orderby o.Id select $"{c.Name}: {o.Total}"
For spending, try customers.Select(c => new { c.Name, Total = orders.Where(...).Sum(o => o.Total) }) then sort and format.
